inputs.text: [happily] Listen close, Wex: we're moving forward in time again. [excited] Dry land, though, is still completely bare.
[curious] Completely bare? No plants at all?
[calm] Not yet, but it's coming: mosses, then the very first green plants appear on the continents. [softly] And soon, [happily] the very first trees.
[amazed] And in the sea, what's happening?
[excited] In the sea, this time is called the Devonian. [serious] It comes from Devon, a region in England where scientists found its rocks. [happily] People call it "the age of fishes."
[playful][calm] Because there are fish of every shape! [amazed] And some of them have thick, fleshy fins, [gasps] almost like legs.
[curious] Almost like legs? Like this one, Tiktaalik?
[happily][excited] Exactly! Tiktaalik can even lift its head out of the water, [pauses] to look around.
[serious][softly] And one day, some of these fish dare to come out completely. [pauses] The very first amphibians are born: animals that live in water AND on land, [calm] like frogs today.
[amazed] And after that, does it become a giant forest?
[chuckles][happily] Almost! A bit later comes the Carboniferous, [serious] named that way because it formed the coal we still use today. [excited] Huge forests, air rich in oxygen...
[amazed] And giant insects flying between the trees!
[playful][calm] A dragonfly as big as a dinner tray, Wex. [pauses] Life on land is only just beginning.
